title: SSC Selection Post Xii 2024 History PART-2

questions.question: Who among the following got defeated by Babur at Chanderi in 1528?
questions.solution:
• Battle of Chanderi (1528): Medini Rai
  • Conquest: Babur captured the strategic fort of Chanderi from the Rajput ruler Medini Rai.

questions.question: The Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur iron ore belt lies in ______ states.
questions.solution:
• Durg-Bastar Belt: Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra
  • Mining: This belt produces high-grade hematite iron ore, largely exported to Japan and South Korea.

questions.question: Who requested the Syrian king to send a Greek philosopher?
questions.solution:
• Bindusara's Request: Bindusara
  • Greek Ties: He requested Antiochus I of Syria for sweet wine, dried figs, and a sophist (philosopher).

questions.question: Who among the following was the guru of Tansen?
questions.solution:
• Tansen's Guru: Swami Haridasa
  • Music: Haridasa was a great saint-musician of the Bhakti movement who taught the legendary Tansen.

questions.question: Guntapalle Chaitya Buddhist cave is situated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
• Guntapalle Cave: Andhra Pradesh
  • Site: Known as the 'Ajanta of Andhra', it contains both circular and rectangular chaityas.

questions.question: The All-India Muslim League, popularly known as the Muslim League, was founded in _________.
questions.solution:
• Muslim League Foundation: 1906
  • Location: Founded at Dhaka under the leadership of Aga Khan and Salimullah Khan.

questions.question: _____________ was elected as the president of the third session of Indian National Congress.
questions.solution:
• Third Session President: Badruddin Tyabji
  • 1887: He was the first Muslim President of the Indian National Congress (Madras Session).

questions.question: In which of the following years, was the Self-Respect movement started in Tamil Nadu region?
questions.solution:
• Self-Respect Movement: 1925
  • Periyar: E.V. Ramaswamy started this to achieve a society where backward castes have equal human rights.

questions.question: Amaravati stupa is situated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
• Amaravati Stupa: Andhra Pradesh
  • Art: Known for its distinctive white marble carvings and relief sculptures.

questions.question: Sher khan defeated Humayun in the battle of Chausa and Kanauj and forced him to flee to _______.
questions.solution:
• Humayun's Exile: Iran
  • 1540: After losing the Battle of Kanauj to Sher Shah Suri, Humayun spent 15 years in exile in the Safavid court of Persia (Iran).

questions.question: Barabar Cave, famously known for depicting Ashokas' inscription, is situated at_______.
questions.solution:
• Barabar Caves: Gaya, Bihar
  • Mauryan: These are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India, gifted by Ashoka to the Ajivika sect.

questions.question: In 1883, which of the following allowed Indians to try Europeans in courts of law?
questions.solution:
• Ilbert Bill (1883): Ilbert Bill
  • Controversy: It sought to remove racial discrimination in the judiciary, but was heavily opposed by the British community.

questions.question: Stupa is a symbol of which of the following religions?
questions.solution:
• Stupa Religion: Buddhism
  • Symbolism: It represents the burial mound of the Buddha and the path to enlightenment.

questions.question: Which Mughal rulers intervention in the succession and internal politics of the Rathor Rajputs of Marwar led to their rebellion?
questions.solution:
• Aurangzeb & Marwar: Aurangzeb
  • Revolt: His refusal to recognize Ajit Singh as the ruler of Marwar sparked a long-term war with the Rajputs.

questions.question: What was the name of the first dynasty that ruled over Magadh kingdom?
questions.solution:
• First Magadh Dynasty: Haryanka dynasty
  • Rulers: Founded by Bimbisara, followed by Ajatashatru.

questions.question: The Prevention of Seditious Meetings Act was passed in __________ by colonial Government.
questions.solution:
• Seditious Meetings Act: 1907
  • Repression: Passed to curb the growing Swadeshi and revolutionary movements in Punjab and Bengal.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts provided the title of the Viceroy to the Governor-General of India?
questions.solution:
• Viceroy Title: Government of India Act, 1858
  • Shift: Following the 1857 revolt, the company was abolished, and the Governor-General became the Crown's representative (Viceroy).

questions.question: During the reign of which of the Pallava kings was the shore temple at Mahabalipuram built?
questions.solution:
• Shore Temple Builder: Narasimhavarman II
  • Ruler: Also known as Rajasimha. The temple at Mahabalipuram is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

questions.question: After the revolt of 1857, the Peel Commission was set up to make recommendations on the ________ reorganisation of British India.
questions.solution:
• Peel Commission: Military
  • Reform: It recommended a 'divide and rule' policy in the army to prevent another 1857-style organized revolt.

questions.question: The Sisodiya ruler of Mewar, Amar Singh, accepted Mughal service during the reign of ___________.
questions.solution:
• Amar Singh's Submission: Jahangir
  • 1615: Jahangir finally brought an end to the long Mughal-Mewar conflict through a respectful treaty.

questions.question: Which of the following rulers was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya in the Battle of Pataliputra?
questions.solution:
• Defeat of Dhana Nanda: Dhana Nanda
  • Maurya Rise: Chandragupta Maurya, with Chanakya's help, overthrew the last Nanda ruler to establish the Mauryan Empire.

questions.question: The historic Salt March was started by Mahatma Gandhi and his followers from ________.
questions.solution:
• Salt March Origin: Sabarmati Ashram
  • 1930: The 240-mile journey ended at Dandi where Gandhi broke the salt law.

questions.question: Rajataranagini, the book authored by Kalhana in 12th Century was originally written in which of the following languages?
questions.solution:
• Rajatarangini Language: Sanskrit
  • History: It is a metrical legend of the kings of Kashmir.

questions.question: How many Mahajanapadas were there during the age of Buddha?
questions.solution:
• 16 Mahajanapadas: 16
  • Source: The Anguttara Nikaya (Buddhist text) and Bhagavati Sutra (Jain text) mention these 16 states.

questions.question: All India Kisan Sabha was founded in 1936 at Indian National Congress (INC) __________ Session as All India Kisan Congress.
questions.solution:
• All India Kisan Sabha: Lucknow
  • Leaders: Founded by Sahajanand Saraswati and N.G. Ranga.
